root_cause.text: The nft_set_rbtree overlap detection in __nft_rbtree_insert incorrectly skipped validation for anonymous-set interval start elements, allowing overlapping intervals when two start elements had the same/lower-bound key and one start fell between an existing interval’s start and end.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “the existing partial overlap detection logic skips anonymous set checks on start elements” and that this permits overlaps like “A-B, A-C where C < B”; the patch restores this check by adding a special anonymous-set case that looks at the previous active element (`nft_rbtree_prev_active(rbe_le)`) and returns `-ENOTEMPTY` if that previous element is an interval end.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add helper support for retrieving the previous active rb-tree element during set insertion to ensure correct handling of anonymous sets.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, nft_rbtree_prev_active(), was added to return the previous rb-tree element via rb_prev() or NULL if none exists, along with a comment stating it is only for anonymous sets where updates are not allowed and all elements are active. In __nft_rbtree_insert(), a new local variable rbe_prev was also added to the nft_rbtree_elem pointer declarations.
intent_record.how: This introduces a dedicated way for insertion logic to access the previous active element in the rb-tree, preparing __nft_rbtree_insert() to use an explicitly tracked predecessor instead of relying only on existing lower/greater neighbor variables. At runtime this enables correct predecessor-based handling for anonymous sets where all elements are active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix anonymous set interval insertion to reject partial overlaps when a new start element falls between an existing start and end.
intent_record.what: The insertion check for consecutive interval start elements was rewritten from a single conditional that rejected them only for non-anonymous sets into a nested block that always detects the case where both the existing lower-or-equal element and the new element are interval starts; within that block, non-anonymous sets still return -ENOTEMPTY immediately, while anonymous sets now additionally compute rbe_prev via nft_rbtree_prev_active(rbe_le) and return -ENOTEMPTY if that previous active element is an interval end.
intent_record.how: At runtime, anonymous sets no longer blindly skip overlap validation when inserting a start element after another start element. The new logic still permits valid consecutive start elements for anonymous constant sets, but prevents insertion when the new start would fall between an existing start and end pair, thereby detecting and rejecting partial interval overlap that was previously missed.

grouping_result.intent: Fix anonymous set interval insertion to reject partial overlaps when a new start element falls between an existing start and end.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix anonymous set interval insertion by correctly detecting overlaps using previous active rb-tree element lookup during insertion.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target anonymous-set interval insertion in nft_set_rbtree and add previous active element lookup to detect and reject overlapping start/end ranges, which matches the described root cause of skipped overlap validation for anonymous-set interval start elements.

candidates.rationale: This condition explicitly disables the overlap check for anonymous sets. The root cause states anonymous-set interval start elements incorrectly skipped validation, which is embodied by gating the check on !nft_set_is_anonymous(set).

This is the enforcement action for rejecting overlapping intervals. Because the preceding condition excludes anonymous sets, this rejection is not triggered when it should be, allowing overlapping intervals.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition is the root cause because it suppresses the overlap validation path for anonymous sets. As a result, anonymous-set interval start elements can bypass the check and be inserted even when they partially overlap an existing interval.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the full overlap-detection logic inside `__nft_rbtree_insert()`, including the anonymous-set handling relevant to the root cause. The vulnerable condition described was that overlap validation was incorrectly skipped for anonymous-set interval start elements, allowing overlapping intervals when two start elements had the same/lower-bound key and one start fell inside an existing interval. In this commit, overlap detection was rewritten to walk ordered nodes and explicitly track the closest less/equal (`rbe_le`) and greater/equal (`rbe_ge`) elements. The key relevant check is: `if (!nft_set_is_anonymous(set) && rbe_le && nft_rbtree_interval_start(rbe_le) && nft_rbtree_interval_start(new)) return -ENOTEMPTY;`. This means anonymous sets intentionally skip the simple consecutive-start rejection, but the function does not stop there; it also performs other overlap checks using `rbe_ge` and `rbe_le`, including exact-overlap detection (`-EEXIST`) and end/end partial-overlap checks. The commit message itself says this change 'Fixes: 7c84d41416d8' and switches to 'node list walk for overlap detection', which is reflected in the new logic: `for (node = first; node != NULL; node = rb_next(node)) { ... }`. Since this version contains the rewritten overlap detection intended to fix the prior tree-descent bug, the vulnerable construct from the root cause is not present here as the old descent-based skip logic has been removed.
